WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000178.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000178.question: How much iodine do we take in - and how much is safe?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000178.answer_short: Americans average 170-250 mcg a day and can sweat out up to 146 mcg; metallic iodine isn't toxic even at 2,000 mcg/day long-term - a wide safety margin.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000181.subject: iodine
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000181.question: What does iodine do through the thyroid?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000181.answer_short: Iodine builds thyroid hormones, which regulate digestion, heart rate, metabolism, temperature and weight - so ~1 million Americans have thyroid trouble.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000185.subject: obscure_elements
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000185.question: What is indium?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000185.answer_short: A rare, soft, bluish-white metal that resists corrosion and 'shrieks' when bent; it is a byproduct of refining zinc. Discovered in 1863 by its bright violet spectral line, it is named from the Latin indicum, 'indigo.'

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000186.subject: obscure_elements
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000186.question: What is iridium?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000186.answer_short: One of the hardest, most corrosion-resistant metals known -- a precious metal like platinum. Smithson Tennant isolated it in 1803 from platinum-ore residues and named it for the Latin iris ('rainbow'), after its vividly colored salts.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000187.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000187.question: Where is potassium found in nature?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000187.answer_short: A positively charged mineral in all soils (highest in alkaline ones); marine plants concentrate it most (52,000 ppm), and in animals it fills the soft tissue.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000188.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000188.question: What is potassium, chemically?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000188.answer_short: A silver-white alkali metal so soft you can cut it with a knife - and is never found pure in nature; Davy first isolated it by electrolysis in 1807.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000189.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000189.question: Is your body slightly radioactive from potassium?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000189.answer_short: A little: 0.012% of natural potassium is radioactive potassium-40, so the ~140 g in your body is a lifelong part of your background radiation.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000190.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000190.question: Where does the name 'potassium' come from?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000190.answer_short: From 'potash' - the potassium-rich ash left when wood and plants are burned in pots; plants were humans' early mineral source, and it's still the main fertilizer.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000191.subject: potassium
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000191.question: What is saltpeter?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000191.answer_short: Potassium nitrate (KNO3) - 'saltpeter,' looks and tastes like salt, used for centuries as a preservative and fertilizer, and one of gunpowder's three ingredients.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000195.subject: krypton
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000195.question: What is krypton - the Superman element?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000195.answer_short: Despite Superman's 'kryptonite,' real krypton is a harmless, unreactive noble gas - which Wallach says 'may in fact be an essential element for all vertebrates.'

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000196.subject: krypton
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000196.question: How was krypton discovered?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000196.answer_short: Noble gases had no place in Mendeleyev's 1869 table; after argon forced a new column, Sir William Ramsay isolated krypton in 1898, naming it from Greek 'kryptos,' hidden.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000197.subject: krypton
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000197.question: Can krypton form compounds - didn't Pauling predict it?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000197.answer_short: Yes - though krypton was thought inert, Linus Pauling used quantum mechanics in 1933 to predict krypton fluoride; Neil Bartlett proved him right by making KrF2 in 1966.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000203.subject: rare_earth_elements
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000203.question: What is lutetium?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000203.answer_short: The last lanthanide -- the hardest, heaviest and one of the least abundant rare earths, silvery-white and corrosion-resistant. Discovered independently in 1907 and named for Lutetia, the ancient name of Paris.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000215.subject: phytates
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000215.question: What are phytates, and which minerals do they block?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000215.answer_short: Phytic acid (inositol hexaphosphate) in whole grains and raw vegetables interferes with absorbing calcium, iron, zinc and other nutrients.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000216.subject: phytates
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000216.question: How does Wallach say to get enough calcium despite phytates?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000216.answer_short: Avoid high-phosphorus/phytate foods (raw vegetables, colas) as much as possible and supplement with plant-derived colloidal and chelated calcium.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000217.subject: sugar
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000217.question: Does sugar, soda, and caffeine affect my calcium and bones?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000217.answer_short: Excess sugar, carbonation and caffeine both cut calcium absorption and leach stored calcium out of the bones.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000218.subject: eggs
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000218.question: Why does Wallach warn against eating raw egg whites?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000218.answer_short: Raw egg white contains avidin, which binds biotin in the gut; 24 raw whites can cause a biotin deficiency (cooking denatures it).

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000219.subject: dairy
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000219.question: What are Wallach's best food sources of vitamin B12, and is pasteurized milk as good?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000219.answer_short: Fresh whole milk, eggs, cheese, muscle meats, liver and kidney; pasteurized and evaporated milk lose 40-90% of their B12.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000220.subject: butter
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000220.question: Is butter or margarine better for your heart?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000220.answer_short: Wallach flips the conventional wisdom: the hydrogenated and partially-hydrogenated vegetable oils (margarine) sold as the safe substitute for butter to prevent arteriosclerosis, atherosclerosis and stroke are now known to be a direct cause of those very diseases — vindicating real butter over its processed replacement.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000221.subject: butter
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000221.question: How much vitamin A is actually in butter?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000221.answer_short: Wallach lists butter as having 165 IU Vitamin A per teaspoon. In the same table (a USDA vitamin-A food table) margarine is listed as having the same amount when fortified, but Wallach's stance is clear: Partially hydrogenated and hydrogenated vegetable oils such as margarine (once sold as the safe substitute for butter to prevent arteriosclerosis, atherosclerosis and stroke) are in fact a direct cause of those diseases, and he tells readers to cook with butter, ghee or mutton fat instead.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000222.subject: beef
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000222.question: Does Wallach think red meat like beef is healthy, or should I avoid it like the vegans say?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000222.answer_short: Wallach flatly rejects the vegan line — he says red meat is healthy and that every long-lived population on earth eats it. In his words, all long-lived peoples eat red meat (pork, beef, goat, lamb), plus poultry, fish, eggs and dairy, and vegans 'lie to themselves' when they insist the world's healthiest people avoid animal products. His warning is concrete: strict vegans who don't supplement minerals correctly tend, within 5 years, to develop grey hair, receding gums, periodontal disease, arthritis, osteoporosis, anemia, hypertension, chronic fatigue, even cancer and liver cirrhosis — because an unsupplemented plant diet leaves them 51 to 57 of the body's essential minerals short (plants can't manufacture minerals).

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000223.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000223.question: Does Wallach think chicken and other poultry belong in a healthy diet, or should we go vegan?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000223.answer_short: Wallach is firmly against going vegan and puts chicken squarely inside a healthy, long-life diet. His core claim: every long-lived population on earth eats animal foods — red meat (pork, beef, goat, lamb), poultry, fish, eggs and dairy — and no vegan, he says, has ever lived to 100 or raised a thriving colony of healthy kids on the diet. Unsupplemented strict vegans, he warns, tend to develop grey hair, receding gums, osteoporosis, anemia, arthritis and even cancer within 5 years, and he points to vegan crusader Linda McCartney, who died at 56 of breast cancer. So poultry isn't something to avoid — it's part of what he sees as a longevity diet, not a food to apologize for.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000224.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000224.question: Is fried chicken okay to eat?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000224.answer_short: Wallach lumps commercial fried chicken in with French fries, fried seafood, high-fructose corn syrup, soft drinks and white flour as things the world's longest-lived ('Blue Zone') peoples have no access to — the frying and processing is the problem, framing fried chicken as a food of ill health.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000225.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000225.question: How can I actually see that bone is made of both calcium and protein?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000225.answer_short: Wallach's kitchen demonstration: soak a chicken drumstick bone in a quart of vinegar for 2 weeks and the acid leaches out the calcium, leaving behind the rubbery protein matrix — showing bone is a protein framework mineralized with calcium, not solid rock.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000226.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000226.question: What can chickens teach us about human joint disease like carpal tunnel?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000226.answer_short: Wallach uses poultry as the model: arsenic plus the B-vitamin choline prevents 100% of perosis ('slipped tendon') in chickens, and the same arsenic deficiency in humans shows up as carpal tunnel syndrome, TMJ and other repetitive-motion joint diseases.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000227.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000227.question: How has chicken been viewed in traditional healing systems?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000227.answer_short: Relaying Taoist Chinese tradition, Wallach notes poultry (with vegetables and fish) is held to nourish the heart, lungs and kidneys, which the Tao relates to fire, metal and water respectively.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000228.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000228.question: What is a pollo-vegetarian?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000228.answer_short: Wallach defines a 'pollo-vegetarian' as really an omnivore who eats poultry on top of grains, vegetables, fruit and nuts — part of his point that most self-described vegetarians actually eat animal foods.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000229.subject: pork
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000229.question: Does Wallach think pork is healthy, or should it be avoided?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000229.answer_short: Wallach counts pork as a legitimate red meat — he points out that every long-lived people on earth eats it, so it is sound animal protein, not a food to shun.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000230.subject: pork
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000230.question: Why does Wallach warn against ham, bacon, and sausage?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000230.answer_short: The nitrates and nitrites cured into processed meats such as ham, bacon, and sausage act as goitrogens, interfering with normal thyroid metabolism and capable of producing thyroid disease.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000231.subject: pork
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000231.question: Do any famously long-lived people eat pork?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000231.answer_short: Yes — and they may be the best example there is. Wallach points to the Okinawans, whom the World Health Organization ranked in 1996 as the longest-lived people in the entire industrialized world, and boiled pork is a staple of their 1,500-calorie daily diet. He puts their life expectancy at 78 years for men and 86 for women, with a documented centenarian rate of 5 per 10,000 people — and, citing the 25-year Okinawa Centenarian Study, he credits their lifestyle and mineral-rich diet, not their genes, for that longevity. Their table alongside the pork includes chicken, eggs, dried minnows, miso and fish soup, tofu, sea and garden vegetables, kelp, garlic, purple sweet potatoes and bitter melon.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000232.subject: eggs
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000232.question: Are eggs a good source of vitamin B12?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000232.answer_short: Wallach lists eggs among the rich dietary sources of vitamin B12, alongside liver, kidney, whole milk, cheese, and muscle meats, relevant because vegans risk B12 deficiency without it.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000234.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000234.question: Has any public figure used the liquid mineral supplement?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000234.answer_short: Wallach cites Nelson Mandela — sharp and animated at his 90th birthday after 27 years imprisoned — taking a liquid plant-derived mineral supplement sent from Atlanta by former UN Ambassador Andrew Young.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000235.subject: orac
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000235.question: What is an ORAC score?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000235.answer_short: A single number rating a food's antioxidant power - the higher the score, the more free-radical damage it can absorb.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000236.subject: orac
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000236.question: Who invented the ORAC test?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000236.answer_short: Scientists at the National Institute on Aging - a division of the NIH in Baltimore - working with Tufts University in Boston.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000237.subject: orac
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000237.question: How does the ORAC test actually work?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000237.answer_short: A fluorescent dye is put in a tube with peroxyl radicals that destroy it; how well the food protects that dye becomes its score.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000238.subject: orac
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000238.question: How many ORAC points should I get a day?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000238.answer_short: 20,000 to 25,000 ORAC points a day - the intake Wallach says is optimal for reaching 100.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000239.subject: orac
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000239.question: Where do ORAC numbers come from?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000239.answer_short: The USDA published ORAC values for 277 commonly eaten American foods in 2007, then a full database in 2008.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000240.subject: antioxidants
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000240.question: Which foods have the highest ORAC score?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000240.answer_short: Ground cloves at 314,446 and cinnamon at 267,536 - spices outscore every fruit by more than tenfold.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000241.subject: orac
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000241.question: Is red wine actually good for you?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000241.answer_short: By ORAC, red beats white by roughly thirteen to one - Cabernet Sauvignon 5,034 against white wine's 392.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000242.subject: orac
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000242.question: How do you pick a good chocolate?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000242.answer_short: Four ways: the percentage of chocolate, the country of origin, the ORAC value, and taste.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000243.subject: free_radicals
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000243.question: What do free radicals actually do to your body?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000243.answer_short: They attack your cells, cell walls and mitochondria - raising the risk of heart disease, cancer, Alzheimer's, cataracts and diabetes, and speeding aging itself.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000244.subject: free_radicals
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000244.question: What causes age spots and liver spots?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000244.answer_short: They're ceroid lipofuscin, the pigment left behind by free-radical damage - and if you have one on the outside, Wallach says you have millions on the inside.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000245.subject: free_radicals
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000245.question: Are age spots a warning sign of something worse?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000245.answer_short: Wallach says yes - how many you have and how dark they are tracks your free-radical damage, and forecasts cataracts, heart disease, diabetes and dementia.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000246.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000246.question: Is aging reversible?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000246.answer_short: On the aging pigment specifically Wallach says yes - and calls the belief that it can't be undone a medical dogma that is simply wrong.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000247.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000247.question: How do you reverse the aging pigment?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000247.answer_short: Cut free-radical foods hard, take every essential nutrient, and push antioxidants to 20,000-25,000 ORAC points a day.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000248.subject: antioxidants
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000248.question: Do antioxidants really help you live longer?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000248.answer_short: Yes for average lifespan, no for the maximum - and only in combination, never one at a time.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000249.subject: antioxidants
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000249.question: What do the world's longest-lived people actually eat?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000249.answer_short: Dark fruits and berries, yellow and red vegetables, cocoa, red wine, green tea and coffee - every day, not occasionally.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000250.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000250.question: What are the four things that get you to 100?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000250.answer_short: Antioxidants, a calorie-restricted diet, mineral-rich food, and avoiding the land mines - leave any one out and Wallach says the whole thing fails.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000251.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000251.question: Can I actually live past 100?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000251.answer_short: Wallach says every human already has the genetic equipment for it - the reasons people don't get there are things they're doing, not things they inherited.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000252.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000252.question: Do I even want to live to 100?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000252.answer_short: Wallach's target isn't extra years in decline - it's reaching past 100 in a beautiful, healthful and functional way.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000253.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000253.question: Do I need good genes to live to 100?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000253.answer_short: No - and good genes won't save you either. Wallach says even if everyone in your family died at 35, you can still make it healthfully to 100.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000254.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000254.question: How many years are we losing?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000254.answer_short: 20 to 25. Wallach says the industrialized world should average 95-100 years and instead averages about 75 - with America falling from 17th in the world to 48th.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000255.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000255.question: How many calories should I eat to live longer?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000255.answer_short: 1,250 to 1,800 a day - but only WITHOUT malnutrition, meaning every essential nutrient at optimal levels inside those calories.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000256.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000256.question: Are minerals more important than vitamins?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000256.answer_short: Wallach's rule: a high-protein, low-carb diet is forgiving of low vitamins but unforgiving of low minerals.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000257.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000257.question: Where did the world's longest-lived people get their minerals?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000257.answer_short: Glacial milk, river silt, rock dust and wood ashes - not a supplement aisle. The ground they ate from still had the minerals in it.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000258.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000258.question: What will stop me reaching 100 no matter what else I do?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000258.answer_short: Wallach's land mines: smoking, excess alcohol, street or prescription drugs, fried foods, burnt meat, sugar and super-heated carbs.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000259.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000259.question: How many more years can I actually add?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000259.answer_short: Wallach calculates 25 to 50 additional HEALTHFUL years for a 150-175 lb person - and says it saves money, because cheaper food offsets the supplements.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000260.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000260.question: How long can a person actually live?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000260.answer_short: Wallach: "who is to say we can't live to be 150, 175 or 200 - we believe we can!" He lists the four-minute mile and the moon landing as things the experts also called impossible.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000261.subject: free_radicals
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000261.question: How much of a brain cell fills with aging pigment as you get older?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000261.answer_short: By Adelman's data Wallach cites, ceroid lipofuscin fills about 35% of a brain cell at age 30-40, 41% by 50-60, 55% by 70-80, and 78% by 90-100.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000262.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000262.question: How far has American longevity fallen in the world rankings?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000262.answer_short: By CDC/WHO surveys, the US fell from 17th in the world in 1990 to 24th by 2000, 46th by 2005, and 48th by 2008.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000265.subject: detox
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000265.question: Does selenium protect against mercury and heavy-metal poisoning?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000265.answer_short: Selenium is a direct antagonist of mercury; Wallach tells anyone exposed to it — dental amalgams, industrial pollution — to supplement selenium before, during, and after any detox.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000266.subject: detox
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000266.question: What is EDTA chelation and where did it come from?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000266.answer_short: Calcium EDTA was invented in Germany just before WWI to antidote arsenic and lead from chemical warfare; the same agent now does IV chelation to clear obstructed arteries.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000267.subject: free_radicals
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000267.question: What are free radicals and why are they dangerous?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000267.answer_short: The gerontologist Roy Walford called free radicals 'the great white sharks in the biochemical sea' — short-lived but voracious molecules that oxidize and damage tissue, especially cell and mitochondrial membranes.

WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000268.subject: antioxidants
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000268.question: What are antioxidants?
WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000268.answer_short: Antioxidants are the body's defense against free radicals — but Wallach's key point is they can't work without minerals: your antioxidant enzymes need cofactors like selenium (for glutathione) to run at full strength.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000080.subject: diabetes
WAL-CLM-LETS-000080.question: Can a normal blood test miss diabetes?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000080.answer_short: Yes — a single fasting blood-sugar reading misses most diabetes and hypoglycemia; Wallach says only a six-hour glucose tolerance test reveals them.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000083.subject: macrobiotics
WAL-CLM-LETS-000083.question: Why does the macrobiotic (brown-rice) diet work?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000083.answer_short: Wallach's take: its successes come mostly from accidentally cutting gluten - people with hidden celiac disease finally absorb minerals, vitamins and fats. The value is nutritional, not the yin/yang theory.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000084.subject: light_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000084.question: What does ultraviolet (UV) light therapy treat?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000084.answer_short: Wallach says UV light boosts vitamin D and the immune system, and treats sore throats, vaginitis, ringworm, athlete's foot and eczema.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000085.subject: light_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000085.question: How is infrared light therapy done?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000085.answer_short: A local immune boost - shine infrared (a heat lamp) on a trigger point through a 1 cm hole until it reddens, drawing in white cells to help chronic wounds, bedsores and arthritis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000086.subject: light_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000086.question: Is UV light therapy safe for the eyes?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000086.answer_short: Therapeutic UV is 'cool' (no heat) and helps skin diseases and arthritis while killing germs - but it can burn the eyes, so wear goggles or don't look at the lamp.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000087.subject: light_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000087.question: How does UV therapy actually work?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000087.answer_short: Its rays span 500-3,100 Angstroms, peaking at 2,537 - the wavelength that gives UV its germicidal, skin-reddening and vitamin-D-making power; visible light is only ~5% of the output.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000088.subject: chiropractic
WAL-CLM-LETS-000088.question: What is chiropractic?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000088.answer_short: A drug-free, surgery-free physical medicine holding that many ills come from 'subluxations' (misaligned vertebrae) pressing on spinal nerves - the West's most accepted alternative therapy.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000089.subject: chiropractic
WAL-CLM-LETS-000089.question: Where does chiropractic come from?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000089.answer_short: Spinal manipulation is ancient (Egypt, China, Babylon); it reached the West in 1895 when D.D. Palmer cured a janitor's deafness, and chiropractors won a 1987 antitrust case against the AMA.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000090.subject: somatic_therapies
WAL-CLM-LETS-000090.question: What is osteopathy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000090.answer_short: A manipulation-based healing art of body and spine, founded ~130 years ago by engineer Andrew Still after he lost all three children to orthodox medicine; today most D.O.s practice much like M.D.s.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000091.subject: somatic_therapies
WAL-CLM-LETS-000091.question: What is reflexology, and how is it meant to work?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000091.answer_short: An ancient Chinese and East Indian system: 'zones' on the soles and palms map to the internal organs, so 10-30 minutes of thumb compression on a point is meant to treat the organ it stands for.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000092.subject: somatic_therapies
WAL-CLM-LETS-000092.question: What is Rolfing (structural integration)?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000092.answer_short: A deep, uncomfortable connective-tissue massage devised by Ida Rolf to break down 'pathological' tissue and correct posture - said to leave patients half an inch to an inch taller.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000093.subject: aromatherapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000093.question: What is aromatherapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000093.answer_short: Massage with plant essential oils (from roots, flowers, leaves, bark, resin); Wallach says they act as pesticides, fungicides and hormone-like agents and help scars, acne and stretch marks.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000094.subject: aromatherapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000094.question: What are specific essential oils used for?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000094.answer_short: Wallach's list: Mexican yam for birth control, sarsaparilla for testosterone, peppermint for intestinal spasm, calamus to lower blood pressure, lemon as an expectorant, and hops/fennel for estrogens.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000095.subject: ayurveda
WAL-CLM-LETS-000095.question: What is Ayurveda, and how old is it?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000095.answer_short: Possibly the most ancient medical art - 'ayur' (life) + 'veda' (science), recorded ~1200 BC. 80-90% of Indians use it, and Wallach says the Greeks (even Pythagoras) learned medicine from the East Indians.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000096.subject: ayurveda
WAL-CLM-LETS-000096.question: How does Ayurveda explain health and disease?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000096.answer_short: The body is seven tissues (Dhatus) kept in balance by food, so 'wrong food' causes disease; it works with the energies Pitta, Kapha and Vaya and five elements, treating imbalances rather than diagnoses.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000097.subject: homeopathy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000097.question: What are Schuessler cell salts (Biochemics)?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000097.answer_short: A 19th-century system from Dr. Wilhelm Schuessler, who analyzed the ash of cremated bodies and found twelve mineral 'salts' he called essential to health; given in homeopathic (highly diluted) doses. Later workers added ~30 trace elements.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000098.subject: homeopathy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000098.question: What are Bach flower remedies?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000098.answer_short: Homeopathic-style flower preparations from bacteriologist Edward Bach (1880-1936), who first collected sun-warmed flower dew; aimed at emotional imbalance rather than physical disease, taken as four drops four times a day.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000099.subject: color_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000099.question: What is color therapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000099.answer_short: Using colored lights or panels for a healing effect — recorded in ancient Egypt and used in Ayurvedic and Chinese medicine; Wallach frames it as a form of light therapy.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000100.subject: color_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000100.question: What does each color treat in color therapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000100.answer_short: Wallach's color map: blue for blood pressure, fever, cuts and burns; red for low blood pressure; orange for stones; yellow for diabetes; green for ulcers, colds and breast cancer.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000101.subject: color_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000101.question: How is color therapy actually done?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000101.answer_short: Six techniques — the Kilner diagnostic screen, reading tissue colors, sun-charged salt bags, colored foods, 'rainbow' sun-charged water, and meditative color breathing.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000102.subject: faith_healing
WAL-CLM-LETS-000102.question: What is faith healing (laying-on-of-hands)?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000102.answer_short: Using a person to mediate healing through belief - recorded in ancient China and Egypt and in Christianity today. Wallach notes 20-60% of patients improve on placebo when positive thought is induced.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000103.subject: faith_healing
WAL-CLM-LETS-000103.question: Who are the Christian Scientists, and what is 'therapeutic touch'?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000103.answer_short: A Christian sect founded in 1879 by Mary Baker Eddy that holds 'healing is proof of God's love'; Wallach says they outlive other Westerners (and get lower insurance rates). Its modern nursing form is 'therapeutic touch.'

WAL-CLM-LETS-000104.subject: herbal_medicine
WAL-CLM-LETS-000104.question: What is herbal medicine?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000104.answer_short: An ancient system using plants to prevent and cure disease - the root of Chinese, Ayurvedic, American Indian and naturopathic medicine, traced back to Chinese pharmacopeias around 3000 BC.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000105.subject: herbal_medicine
WAL-CLM-LETS-000105.question: Do real drugs come from herbs?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000105.answer_short: Yes - Wallach notes over 30% of orthodox pharmaceuticals derive from plants (digitalis from foxglove, the cancer drug vincristine from periwinkle), and praises herbs' relative safety and millennia of use.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000106.subject: hydrotherapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000106.question: What is hydrotherapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000106.answer_short: Healing with water - practiced since Roman times across all medicine, from sitz baths for hemorrhoids to whirlpools for injuries and mineral baths for arthritis; insurance often covers it if prescribed.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000107.subject: hydrotherapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000107.question: What are the different kinds of hydrotherapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000107.answer_short: Cold baths cut swelling; hot baths ease soreness; mineral baths help arthritis; steam baths detox heavy metals; sitz baths for hemorrhoids; epsom for edema; water fasts and colonics for detox.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000108.subject: negative_ion_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000108.question: What is negative ion therapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000108.answer_short: Using negatively charged air particles to prevent and treat disease - abundant in forests and at the beach (300-1,000 per cubic meter) but low in AC'd rooms; too many POSITIVE ions bring anxiety and depression.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000109.subject: negative_ion_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000109.question: What does negative ion therapy do?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000109.answer_short: Six effects - it lowers heart rate/BP, deepens breathing, speeds respiratory cilia, boosts glands and steadies brain rhythm - and Wallach says it especially helps asthma, allergies and cystic fibrosis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000110.subject: urine_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000110.question: What is urine therapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000110.answer_short: Injecting a patient's own urine back into them to boost immunity - the same idea as an allergist's shots; Wallach says MD allergists used it for 50 years until prepared allergens became profitable.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000111.subject: urine_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000111.question: How is urine therapy performed?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000111.answer_short: Urine is centrifuged and filtered to remove cells and bacteria, then 5-10 mL is injected under the skin (procaine stops any sting); Wallach cites use for allergies, asthma, migraine and arthritis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000112.subject: homeopathy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000112.question: What is homeopathy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000112.answer_short: A system on two principles: 'like cures like' (a substance that causes symptoms in the healthy can cure a disease with those symptoms) and 'minimum dose' - using extremely diluted preparations.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000113.subject: homeopathy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000113.question: Who founded homeopathy, and does the dilution really work?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000113.answer_short: Samuel Hahnemann, who found Cinchona bark gave healthy people malaria-like symptoms; oddly, more dilute often meant a stronger effect - though past about 12C not one molecule of the original remains.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000114.subject: naturopathy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000114.question: What is naturopathy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000114.answer_short: A whole system of natural medicine (N.D.) built on 'FIRST DO NO HARM' and the body's own healing power - covering herbs, hydrotherapy, homeopathy, nutrition and natural childbirth, but not major surgery or most drugs.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000115.subject: macrobiotics
WAL-CLM-LETS-000115.question: Where did macrobiotics come from?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000115.answer_short: George Ohsawa created it in 1946 Japan, using it to heal his own tuberculosis, then opened a healing center and toured the world teaching a philosophy of health through eating.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000116.subject: macrobiotics
WAL-CLM-LETS-000116.question: What is the macrobiotic diet?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000116.answer_short: An eating system built on balancing 'yin' (fruit, drinks, sweet) and 'yang' (meat, grains, dense) foods; reported to help food allergies, diabetes and - when wheat is dropped - grain sensitivity.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000117.subject: vitamins
WAL-CLM-LETS-000117.question: What is megavitamin (orthomolecular) therapy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000117.answer_short: Using vitamins at very high 'pharmacologic' doses - the 1968 'megavitamin theory' that Linus Pauling named 'orthomolecular medicine' and Abram Hoffer extended to psychiatry, reportedly for colds, depression and schizophrenia, though orthodoxy never endorsed it.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000122.subject: digestion
WAL-CLM-LETS-000122.question: What happens if you don’t fix low stomach acid?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000122.answer_short: Untreated achlorhydria costs you B-12, calcium and protein, and brings on new food allergies as half-digested protein fragments get absorbed. Treatment is 75–250 mg betaine HCl 15–20 minutes before each meal, or 1–2 oz of vinegar with gentian if you have none.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000137.subject: digestion
WAL-CLM-LETS-000137.question: Why isn’t my B12 supplement working?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000137.answer_short: Because vitamin B12 needs stomach acid to be absorbed at all. In Wallach’s anemia program the betaine hydrochloride comes first — 75–200 mg three times a day, 15–20 minutes before meals — specifically to assure B-12 absorption, before the B12 itself.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000165.subject: digestion
WAL-CLM-LETS-000165.question: How do I get rid of bloating and gas?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000165.answer_short: Wallach treats the missing acid, not the gas: oral hydrogen peroxide diluted at 20 drops per ounce, 1 ounce twice a day, plant-derived colloidal minerals, and betaine hydrochloride with pancreatic enzymes at 75–200 mg three times a day, 15 minutes before meals.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000173.subject: digestion
WAL-CLM-LETS-000173.question: Should I take enzymes with food or between meals?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000173.answer_short: Both, for different jobs. Before meals they digest your food; taken between meals on an empty stomach, Wallach says pancreatic enzymes get into your bloodstream and dissolve blood clots — which is why his bruise protocol puts them at 200 mg three times a day between meals.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000194.subject: urine_therapy
WAL-CLM-LETS-000194.question: How do autoimmune urine and blood therapies work?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000194.answer_short: They rev the body's defenses against foreign substances - including cancer proteins - much the way allergy shots build tolerance to pollen.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000209.subject: gluten
WAL-CLM-LETS-000209.question: What does celiac disease do to absorption, and can the gut heal?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000209.answer_short: Wheat gluten can destroy up to 70% of the intestine's absorptive surface (90% by age 45–50). Wallach says removing the offending grain lets the gut repair over 90 days.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000232.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000232.question: Why were midwives who knew contraception called witches?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000232.answer_short: Wallach notes midwives who knew contraception herbs were once branded 'witches' and burned; he ranks birth control (abstinence, barriers, hormones - least desirable, IUDs, surgery) and bluntly calls sex outside marriage 'Russian roulette.'

WAL-CLM-LETS-000245.subject: gluten
WAL-CLM-LETS-000245.question: How long does it take to heal your gut?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000245.answer_short: 60 to 90 days. That is how long Wallach tells dermatitis patients to expect before the intestinal lesions heal to the point where they can absorb nutrients efficiently — on a gluten-free, cow’s-milk-free diet with digestive aids.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000255.subject: digestion
WAL-CLM-LETS-000255.question: How do you treat dumping syndrome?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000255.answer_short: With bitters and buffering rather than more acid: classic bitters such as gentian, folic acid at 3–5 mg a day, pectin at half an ounce in water before meals, high-animal-protein food, and lying down for half an hour after eating.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000263.subject: sexual_health
WAL-CLM-LETS-000263.question: How does Wallach approach premature ejaculation?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000263.answer_short: He calls it normal and curable, with causes (high expectation, infrequent sex, friction) not guilt; his fix is comfort with each other's bodies, frequent sex, and good lubrication, with ginseng and Zumbani as tonics.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000312.subject: vaccines
WAL-CLM-LETS-000312.question: What is Wallach's stance on vaccine mandates?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000312.answer_short: He calls immunization 'the greatest interface between government and freedom of choice,' opposes compulsory school mandates, defends the religious exemption, and warns that many vaccination programs have carried catastrophic diseases.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000347.subject: longevity
WAL-CLM-LETS-000347.question: How long can humans live?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000347.answer_short: Wallach says 120-130 years, vs the ~72-78 of actuary tables. He credits the Hunza's ~100-year average to plant-derived colloidal minerals, and says filters, digestive aids and the baseline program add ~20 years.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000352.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-LETS-000352.question: If someone can't absorb nutrients from food, what's the best way to get minerals in?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000352.answer_short: Liquid plant-derived colloidal minerals, Wallach says — the most efficient way to get minerals into malnourished people. He frames malnutrition-from-malabsorption (celiac changes or low stomach acid) as the common denominator of almost all degenerative disease, so the absorbable colloidal form is his answer.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000362.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000362.question: What is 'metabolic therapy'?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000362.answer_short: Wallach's umbrella term for curing disease by fixing whole-body metabolism - through nutrition, herbs, homeopathy, acupuncture, manipulation and hydrotherapy.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000370.subject: home_remedies
WAL-CLM-LETS-000370.question: How can you repel mosquitoes naturally?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000370.answer_short: Screen doors and 'zapper' lights set 15-25 yards from the house draw mosquitoes off; Wallach adds pennyroyal oil on the skin and vitamin B1 at 500 mg/day as natural repellents - handy since mosquitoes carry malaria and encephalitis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000467.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000467.question: Is a hospital birth necessary?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000467.answer_short: Wallach says pregnancy is normal, not a disease, and home birth is the safest, cheapest option - he delivered ~200 babies at home with one c-section, and blames the 35% hospital c-section rate on economics.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000468.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000468.question: What prenatal care can a woman do herself?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000468.answer_short: A lot: self breast and pelvic exams, cycle tracking, home pregnancy tests, OTC prenatal vitamins, own blood-pressure and urine tests - and, barring a few specific risks, she can give birth at home.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000469.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000469.question: What birth control can you buy without a prescription?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000469.answer_short: Condoms, spermicidal creams, jellies, foams and sponges - all over the counter. Wallach considers these barrier methods much safer than IUDs (the Dalkon Shield) and the pill (clots, deaths, sterility).

WAL-CLM-LETS-000470.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000470.question: What causes most birth defects?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000470.answer_short: Wallach's 'pet peeve': 98% come from nutritional deficiencies, not radiation. Teens have more than women over 40 - and lab animals get defect-free diets, so why feed a rat better than a pregnant woman?

WAL-CLM-LETS-000471.subject: cystic_fibrosis
WAL-CLM-LETS-000471.question: Is cystic fibrosis really genetic?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000471.answer_short: Wallach's signature thesis: no - it's a selenium and essential-fatty-acid deficiency from the mother's malabsorption. He cites 1972 Cornell chicks cured in 21 days by selenium, and 450 patients treated since 1978.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000472.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000472.question: Is infertility a nutrition problem?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000472.answer_short: Wallach says mostly yes - as a breeder feeds a mare 120 days before mating, he's reversed hundreds of cases by nourishing both partners; one 'infertile' doctor had vitamin A at 10% of normal (malabsorption).

WAL-CLM-LETS-000473.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000473.question: How should you choose a medical specialist?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000473.answer_short: Only when truly needed - then get three-plus opinions from different fields, ask to speak with ten past patients, and start conservative; the more 'exotic' the specialist, the higher the risk.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000474.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000474.question: How impaired are conventional doctors?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000474.answer_short: Wallach cites alarming numbers - tens of thousands of physician alcoholics, heavy drug use among doctors and students, and the U.S. losing 'seven medical-school classes' a year to addiction and suicide.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000475.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000475.question: What does Wallach mean by 'be your own doctor'?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000475.answer_short: Become your own primary care provider - you're unlikely to harm yourself. Try conservative and alternative care before orthodox medicine, and 'separate medicine and state.'

WAL-CLM-LETS-000476.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000476.question: What's the best health insurance?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000476.answer_short: Not getting sick. Prevention - a baseline supplement program and daily self-care - is cheaper and easier than illness; Wallach calls it the best buy for your health dollars.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000477.subject: hospital_dangers
WAL-CLM-LETS-000477.question: How dangerous are hospitals?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000477.answer_short: Wallach's tally: 970 of 1,000 hospitals billed wrong (always in their favor), up to half of new equipment defective on arrival, and 100,000+ deaths a year from hospital-caught infections.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000478.subject: hospital_dangers
WAL-CLM-LETS-000478.question: What should you do if you're hospitalized?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000478.answer_short: Have a family member stay to check every shot, pill and procedure before it's given, confirm your IV lines, and use family blood if needed - just as orthodox doctors monitor their own families.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000479.subject: hospital_dangers
WAL-CLM-LETS-000479.question: What is the 'medical industrial Bermuda Triangle'?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000479.answer_short: Wallach's name for the FDA, AMA and drug companies - costing Americans more than national defense while the U.S. ranks 17th in longevity and 32nd in birth defects. He calls to 'separate Medicine and State.'

WAL-CLM-LETS-000480.subject: pregnancy_birth
WAL-CLM-LETS-000480.question: Which agency said women should supplement before pregnancy?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000480.answer_short: The CDC, in 1992 - not the FDA. Wallach credits the CDC's independence from company revenue, and notes it independently echoed his own preconception-supplementation thesis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000481.subject: be_your_own_doctor
WAL-CLM-LETS-000481.question: How do you take charge of your home environment?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000481.answer_short: Grow some food and treat your home water and air - Wallach says 3,000+ mostly-carcinogenic chemicals slip through city water (clear isn't safe); a bone-charcoal filter removes them.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000482.subject: phytates
WAL-CLM-LETS-000482.question: Can phytates block even supplemented calcium?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000482.answer_short: Yes — Wallach calls phytates a natural chelating substance in plants that can make even supplemented calcium unavailable.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000483.subject: carbonated_beverages
WAL-CLM-LETS-000483.question: Are carbonated soft drinks bad for you, even diet soda?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000483.answer_short: Cut sugar and caffeine, and drop soft drinks; even diet sodas are full of phosphates that drive osteoporosis.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000484.subject: beef
WAL-CLM-LETS-000484.question: Is there any condition where Wallach says to avoid beef entirely?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000484.answer_short: Yes. For lupus (SLE), Wallach explicitly says to avoid beef, along with dairy and alfalfa, as part of treatment.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000485.subject: beef
WAL-CLM-LETS-000485.question: Is it dangerous to eat rare or undercooked beef?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000485.answer_short: Wallach warns that rare beef can transmit toxoplasmosis, especially dangerous for pregnant women because the infection will cause birth defects in the fetus — brain defects, blindness and mental retardation.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000486.subject: pork
WAL-CLM-LETS-000486.question: Can eating pork trigger a gallbladder attack?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000486.answer_short: Yes. Wallach says pork ranks close behind eggs and onions as a food that precipitates gallbladder attacks.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000487.subject: pork
WAL-CLM-LETS-000487.question: Can you get parasites or tapeworms from pork?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000487.answer_short: Yes. Wallach warns that raw pork is one of the foods that transmits tapeworm; the encysted larvae hatch in the gut and latch onto the intestinal wall.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000488.subject: fish
WAL-CLM-LETS-000488.question: How does fish oil help cholesterol / heart health?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000488.answer_short: The EPA in fish oil (and flax oil) raises protective HDL cholesterol — the fraction that ferries cholesterol to the liver for disposal — while refined sugar drives HDL down to dangerous levels.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000489.subject: detox
WAL-CLM-LETS-000489.question: Do supplements help protect against heavy metals and pollution?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000489.answer_short: Wallach says plant-derived colloidal minerals do double duty — preventing disease and reducing your risk of damage from heavy metals and pollution in the environment.

WAL-CLM-LETS-000490.subject: detox
WAL-CLM-LETS-000490.question: How does Wallach say to reduce my exposure to environmental toxins?
WAL-CLM-LETS-000490.answer_short: Take control of your household environment: grow some of your own organic food and filter your home's water and air — a bone-charcoal filter, he says, removes hydrocarbons and heavy metals.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000024.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000024.question: Which peoples actually live to 120–140, and how?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000024.answer_short: Wallach names several ancient, diverse cultures — Tibetans, Georgians, Armenians, Azerbaijanis, Abkhazians, Hunzakuts, Vilcabambas and the Titicacas — who reach a disease-free 120–140 years by getting their minerals as plant-derived colloidal minerals (his plant 'rare earths').

WAL-CLM-RARE-000059.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000059.question: What's the actual secret behind the long-lived 'Age Beater' cultures?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000059.answer_short: Eating plants rich in organic plant-derived colloidal minerals. The plants pull inorganic minerals from 'Glacial Milk' and convert them into the cell-usable colloidal form — the secret Wallach credits to the five 'Age Beater' cultures.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000061.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000061.question: How much more of a plant-derived mineral does the body actually absorb?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000061.answer_short: About 98% of it, on Wallach's account — versus only 8–12% of the same mineral taken as ground-up rock. That gap is the whole reason he insists on the plant-derived (colloidal) form.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000062.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000062.question: What do all five long-lived cultures have in common?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000062.answer_short: One shared practice: they all irrigate their terraced fields with mineral-rich 'Glacial Milk' carrying 60 or more minerals. Wallach calls this the common denominator behind their 120–140-year lifespans — the minerals reaching them as plant-derived colloidal minerals in the crops.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000069.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000069.question: Of the 90 essentials, which ones matter most?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000069.answer_short: His own ranking inside the 90: get a highly usable source of all of them every day — but the most critical, he says, are the plant-derived colloidal minerals. That, on his account, is what the long-lived cultures boil down to.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000070.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000070.question: Where do these minerals come from in the first place?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000070.answer_short: They start as rock. Glaciers grind 2 to 6 inches off the mountain every year into a dust as fine as clay, and the melt water carries it out as “Glacial Milk” — the mineralized water the long-lived cultures flood their fields with.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000071.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000071.question: There are thousands of glaciers — so why only a handful of long-lived cultures?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000071.answer_short: Not the ice — the rock beneath it. Glacial milk carries only what its parent mountain held: the long-lived cultures' glaciers grind rock with 60 to 72 minerals; most of the world's thousands, 3 to 20 — not enough, he says, for longevity.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000072.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000072.question: Do the long-lived cultures drink Glacial Milk, or use it another way?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000072.answer_short: They irrigate with it, not drink it. Wallach says only ~5–12% of the raw metallic minerals in 'Glacial Milk' are absorbable if you drink it — the real key is using it as irrigation water, so plants convert those minerals into the highly usable plant-derived colloidal form.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000073.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000073.question: What benefits do the long-lived cultures get from all those minerals?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000073.answer_short: Freedom from the degenerative diseases, Wallach says. Millennia of irrigating terraces with mineral-rich 'Glacial Milk' leave them without hypertension, heart disease, stroke, aneurysms, arthritis, osteoporosis, dental disease, cataracts, diabetes, cancer or lupus.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000074.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000074.question: Why does the form of a mineral matter so much for absorption?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000074.answer_short: Because absorption efficiency varies enormously by form. Wallach ties it to the gap between how much of a mineral the body truly needs and how much you must eat to get it — for the metallic form the ratio runs from about 1:1 (iodine) to 1:100 (chromium) — so the most efficient form, plant-derived colloidal minerals, should be consumed.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000088.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000088.question: Can plant-derived colloidal minerals help clear heavy metals from the body?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000088.answer_short: Per a study Wallach cites: Gary Price Todd, MD gave patients 3 oz of liquid plant-derived colloidal minerals daily; hair levels of lead, cadmium and mercury first ROSE at three months (the minerals unmask hidden tissue stores), then dropped steadily — a reduction Todd found to be time- and dose-related.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000112.subject: rare_earth_elements
WAL-CLM-RARE-000112.question: Does cerium have a medical use?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000112.answer_short: Yes -- cerium (a rare earth that accumulates in bone) is used as cerium nitrate, a topical disinfectant for severe burn victims.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000276.subject: drug_safety_elderly
WAL-CLM-RARE-000276.question: Which tranquilizers and sleeping pills are risky for older adults?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000276.answer_short: Wallach flags Valium (diazepam), Librium (chlordiazepoxide) and Dalmane (flurazepam) as too long-acting or addictive -- they cause drowsiness, confusion and falls in the elderly. His fix: address the underlying need with minerals (calcium, magnesium, lithium, chromium, vanadium) and cut sugar and caffeine.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000277.subject: drug_safety_elderly
WAL-CLM-RARE-000277.question: What other tranquilizers and sleeping pills should older adults avoid?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000277.answer_short: The second half of Wallach's list: Miltown (meprobamate), Nembutal (pentobarbital) and Seconal (secobarbital) -- all addictive, long-acting and fall-prone. Same mineral replacement: calcium, magnesium, lithium, chromium and vanadium.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000312.subject: salt
WAL-CLM-RARE-000312.question: Does Wallach think salt is bad for you?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000312.answer_short: Wallach calls salt a craved necessity and the universal food condiment; a saltless bread-and-water diet was once a dreaded Dutch punishment.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000313.subject: sugar
WAL-CLM-RARE-000313.question: Why do I crave sugar and soft drinks?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000313.answer_short: Craving soft drinks and sweets is a sign of chromium and vanadium deficiency, not real hunger.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000314.subject: butter
WAL-CLM-RARE-000314.question: What should I cook with instead of margarine or vegetable oil?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000314.answer_short: In his See-Food Diet free-radical-elimination list, Wallach gives a flat cooking directive: no margarine — cook with butter, ghee, mutton fat, or water instead. Butter is on his approved-fats shortlist for the kitchen.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000315.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-RARE-000315.question: Is chicken soup actually useful when you're sick with the flu?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000315.answer_short: Yes. Wallach holds up chicken soup — with the herbs echinacea and goldenseal plus a dose of bismuth — as the safe, effective nutritional way to handle the flu (which he frames as dehydration and diarrhea). His cautionary contrast is George Washington, who had influenza but was killed by his doctors, not the illness: in a little over 12 hours they drained him of 80 to 90 ounces of blood (6 pints), dosed him with calomel (mercury) and emetic tartar (antimony), and blistered his skin and throat, until Washington himself begged to be allowed to die in peace. The lesson Wallach draws is blunt — a grandmother's bowl of chicken soup would have served the 'Father of our Country' better than the best physicians of his day.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000316.subject: chicken
WAL-CLM-RARE-000316.question: What nutrients does chicken provide — is it a source of dietary fat?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000316.answer_short: Wallach lists chicken among the primary food sources of dietary fats/lipids (with pork, fish, beef and lamb), the animal fats that supply energy alongside plant oils, nuts and dairy.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000317.subject: eggs
WAL-CLM-RARE-000317.question: Can eating eggs help with menopause symptoms?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000317.answer_short: Because cholesterol is the raw material the body uses to make estrogen, Wallach says eating 2 eggs every morning supplies that raw material and lets a woman slip through menopause almost symptom-free.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000318.subject: fish
WAL-CLM-RARE-000318.question: Is canned tuna worse than fresh tuna?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000318.answer_short: Canned tuna carries nearly double the lead of fresh tuna, because the sealant used on can seams leaches lead into the food.

WAL-CLM-RARE-000319.subject: colloidal_minerals
WAL-CLM-RARE-000319.question: How is a plant-derived colloidal mineral supplement actually made?
WAL-CLM-RARE-000319.answer_short: Humic shale — prehistoric plants that dried without ever turning to rock — is ground to a flour and soaked in spring water for three to four weeks until it reaches a specific gravity of 3.0. It takes 78 pounds of shale (about 1,034 lb of the original plants) to make one liter of the 98%-absorbable concentrate, carrying 60-plus minerals.
